closures.item: F-D4-01 (a2): the deleted failure-arm clear is genuinely covered by removePerDropState — captured drop deleted mid-gesture, end to end
closures.proof: The deleted line could only matter in a state where `placedDrops[id] == nil && roomDrops[id] == nil && demoDrops has no id` WHILE `editingDropID == id`. That state is unconstructible. Exhaustive grep of every write that can remove a placedDrops entry: `placedDrops[id] = nil` appears at exactly ONE line, :1663, inside removePerDropState; `placedDrops.removeAll()` appears at exactly ONE line, :943, inside resetPlacements. removePerDropState (:1660-1692) does, in one synchronous body: :1663 placedDrops[id]=nil → :1671 liveEditingDrops.remove(id) → :1672-1677 `if editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil; heldGestures = 0 }` → :1684-1687 nearestDrop=nil/nearestDropDistance=nil. resetPlacements (:930-983) does :943 placedDrops.removeAll() → :951-953 liveEditingDrops.removeAll(); editingDropID = nil; heldGestures = 0. WHO clears the capture: removePerDropState :1673. WHO zeroes the counter: :1676, in the same `if`, so the pair can never split. ORDER vs a queued tick: the class is @MainActor (:25-26) and removePerDropState contains no `await` — the three call sites (:732 clearRoomDrops, :1942 pedestrian reconcile, :2491 transit reconcile) all run synchronously inside a main-actor tick, and adjustNearestDrop/applyEdit are main-actor calls from SwiftUI, so no tick can interleave mid-body. End-to-end trace: user drags X (held=1, capture=X, liveEditingDrops={X}) → X leaves the library/radius → next 400 ms tick reaches :1941 `for (id,_) in placedHolders where !seen.contains(id)` → removePerDropState(X) atomically nils capture, zeroes the counter, nils nearestDrop → the finger's next tick hits editTarget(capture: nil, held: false, nearest: nil) at :2048 → nil → `return` at :2050, applyEdit is never entered. The authored callers are also sealed: snapNearestDropToGround :2185 guards `let drop = nearestDrop, let holder = placedHolders[drop.id]`, relocateNearestDrop :2274 the same — both nil after removal. applyEdit's vanish arm is now genuinely dead code, and the deleted clear was redundant, not load-bearing.

closures.item: F-D4-01 (b1): the round-4 two-thumb trace replayed against the NEW code — does B's next tick still bind to the original capture?
closures.proof: Line-by-line on the current file with drops X (nearest) and Y. Thumb A grabs height → ARScreen.swift:504 beginLiveEdit → :452 heldGestures=min(0+1,4)=1; :453 lastLiveEditTickAt=now; :454 editingDropID==nil so capture=X. Thumb B grabs scale → ARScreen.swift:531 beginLiveEdit → held=2; :454 capture non-nil, stays X. A drags → :2048 editTarget(capture:X, held:true, nearest:X)=X; :2051 capture=X; :2052 tick stamp; applyEdit(X, commit:false) → :2100 liveEditingDrops.insert(X). A RELEASES (ARScreen.swift:506, commit:true) → :2048 →X; :2051 capture=X; :2053-2060 commitBookkeeping(heldGestures:2, capture:X, committed:X) → :541 remaining=max(0,1)=1; :542 captureClears = (1==0 && X==X) = FALSE → returns (1, X). So heldGestures=1, editingDropID=X. applyEdit(X, commit:true) persists and touches no gesture state. NEXT 400 ms tick: updateNearest :1694-1698 `guard editingDropID == nil else { return }` — capture is X, so nearest STAYS FROZEN on X even though the geo-nearest is now Y. THUMB B'S NEXT TICK: :2048 editTarget(capture:X, held:true, nearest:X) = X. B binds to the ORIGINAL capture. Y is never touched. B releases → commitBookkeeping(1, X, X) → remaining=0, captureClears=(true && true)=TRUE → (0, nil); capture clears, freeze lifts, next drag re-captures. closures.item: F-D4-01 (b2): authored variant — "Place on ground" tapped mid-drag; does the gesture's capture survive the snap?
closures.proof: The button is confirmed to sit directly under the three sliders in the same VStack (ARScreen.swift:484-579; sliders :489-562, snap button :570-572), so a second thumb can tap it while the first drags. Trace: thumb A drags height on X (held=1, capture=X, liveEditingDrops={X}). Thumb B taps → ARScreen.swift:571 snapNearestDropToGround → :2185 resolves `nearestDrop` which is still X (frozen by the capture at :1698) → :2239 applyEdit(to: X, height: ..., commit: true). applyEdit's body (:2075-2164) contains NO write to editingDropID or heldGestures — so after the snap, capture is STILL X and held is STILL 1. :2241 sets groundLockBaseY[X]. ARScreen.swift:572 syncSliders() re-seeds from nearestDrop, which is still X — correct drop. Thumb A's next tick: :2048 editTarget(capture:X, held:true) = X → keeps editing X; :2100 re-inserts X into liveEditingDrops. Thumb A releases: commitBookkeeping(1, X, X) → (0, nil) — capture clears on the LAST finger, and :2153-2156 clears groundLockBaseY[X] because height != nil, so the deliberate height choice correctly overrides the snap's lock. Under round 4 this same tap nilled the capture, unfreezing :1698 → nearest could flip to Y → ARScreen.swift:601 fired syncSliders() and jumped thumb A's knob under the finger AND A's next tick re-bound to Y. Both halves are gone.

closures.item: F-D4-01 (c)(ii): can `capture` ever be != `id` when commitBookkeeping is called?
closures.proof: No — provably never, at the only call site. :2051 `editingDropID = id` executes unconditionally two statements before :2058, and nothing between them can change it (:2052 only writes lastLiveEditTickAt, and only when !commit). So `capture == id` at :2059 is an invariant, and the `&& capture == id` conjunct at :542 is dead at the call site. This is HARMLESS and the conjunct should NOT be deleted: :2051's unconditional write is load-bearing. Counter-example proving it: if capture were nil and held==2 (both beginLiveEdit calls landed while nearestDrop was nil, :454 no-ops), the first commit resolves via editTarget's `held ? nearest : nil` branch to Y; :2051 then ESTABLISHES capture=Y, which is what freezes :1698 for the surviving second finger. Remove :2051 from the commit path and the second finger would re-derive nearest — the F-D4-01 harm by another door. Recorded as a LOW (F-D5-02) for the dead-conjunct/dead-test-row bookkeeping only, not as a defect.

closures.item: F-D4-01 (c)(iii): cancelLiveEdit zeroing heldGestures while N fingers are down — still correct with the counter?
closures.proof: Correct, and it cannot drive the counter negative. cancelLiveEdit :460-465 sets heldGestures=0 BEFORE the early-return guard at :462, so the counter is zeroed on every entry regardless of the guard. Callers: :441 suspendSession, :640 markCameraHidden, :1225 the 30 s backstop in updatePowerTier. Trace with 2 fingers down: cancel → held=0, capture=nil, liveEditingDrops empty. Finger A moves → :2048 editTarget(capture:nil, held:false, nearest:Y) = nil → :2050 return. The tick is REFUSED (dead slider — the round-3 designed refusal, safe), heldGestures is untouched. Finger A releases → the commit takes the same nil path at :2050 and never reaches :2058, so no decrement below zero. Finger B identical. Net state consistent. The one contrived sequel — cancel, then a THIRD finger presses while A/B are still down (:452 held=1, :454 capture=nearest=Y), after which A's ticks bind to Y — is harmless because the freeze lifted at cancel, so nearestDrop already flipped to Y and ARScreen.swift:601 `.onChange(of: nearestDrop?.id)` already ran syncSliders(), re-seeding A's knob to Y's values. Right drop, right seed.

closures.item: F-D4-01 (c)(i): liveEditingDrops.remove(id) still runs on an AUTHORED commit while a gesture holds the SAME drop — can VPS glide or the governor drop the pin under a live finger?
closures.proof: The window is REAL but benign; keeping insert/remove in applyEdit (the counsel-converged call) survives the trace. Yes, :2152 removes X from liveEditingDrops on the authored commit while held>0, and a stationary finger sends no re-inserting :2100 tick, so the window persists until the next drag movement or slider release. GOVERNOR HALF — INERT: PowerGovernor.swift:62-64 holds `desired = .full` on an independent disjunct `contentInView && nearestRenderedDistance < 60`, which is true by construction (the user is looking at the drop they are editing), and even if it were false, :51/:81-89 impose a 6 s downgradeDelay while the next drag tick re-pins in <400 ms. The pin cannot drop. VPS/COMPASS HALF — bounded and off-axis: the :992 guard and the :1870-1873 compass-skip stop excluding X, so the pedestrian loop can re-position it; but the sliders own height/scale/rotation, NOT position, and :1888 `let y = groundLockBaseY[drop.id] ?? ...` pins Y to the lock that :2241 just wrote, so only x/z can move — and x/z is recomputed to the same GPS-derived target it computes every tick anyway. The one visible motion is the deliberate re-pin the user just asked for (:2157-2161 removes vpsOwnedDrops + invalidateAnchor, so a VPS-owned drop falls back to the compass frame and later re-glides), which happens identically with no finger on the screen; ADR-028's :1898-1903 deferral further suppresses sub-forced in-view slides. Filed as a residual, not a finding.

closures.item: (d) D3 on CommitBookkeepingTests + the edited testEditTargetBindsInBothDirections
closures.proof: See test_vacuity for the per-assertion verdicts. Summary: the two CommitBookkeepingTests are non-vacuous guards on the PURE RULE (XCTAssertEqual(first.capture, capture, "capture must outlive the first commit") at WaveDTests.swift:535 trips if the round-4 rule is re-expressed as `captureClears = capture == id`; XCTAssertEqual(stray.remainingHeld, 0) at :556 trips if the max(0,·) floor at :541 is dropped). But F-D4-01 was never a defect in a rule — it was a WIRING defect, and grep for `GeoARSessionManager(` across AugmentMeRealityTests/ returns ZERO hits, so nothing in the 149-test suite observes editingDropID or heldGestures. Concrete proof of the gap: re-add `if editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil }` to the end of applyEdit's commit block (:2151-2163) while LEAVING commitBookkeeping and its :2058 call exactly as shipped — F-D4-01 is fully restored and all 149 tests stay green. testEditTargetBindsInBothDirections is vacuous AS A GUARD ON THIS ROUND'S EDIT: dropping a parameter that was a literal nil at its one call site is behaviour-preserving by construction, and all four surviving assertions held identically under the round-4 implementation. This is F-D4-CTX unresolved for the fourth consecutive round — see F-D5-03.

findings.claim: The round-5 fix is correct in itself, but it DELETES the accidental self-heal that was the only thing bounding F-D4-SLIDER (round-4 MEDIUM, accepted into the record: the HUD-hide tap and the fireworks-demo teardown remove the Slider from the view tree mid-drag and SwiftUI never delivers onEditingChanged(false), so beginLiveEdit's :452 increment LEAKS). Round 4's applyEdit tail cleared editingDropID on EVERY commit, so one commit always re-armed :1698 and the very next beginLiveEdit re-captured the true nearest (:454). Round 5 makes the capture clear ONLY when the counter reaches 0 (:542), so a single leaked increment pins editingDropID FOREVER: every later gesture takes :454's `editingDropID == nil` false branch, every later tick takes editTarget's `if let capture` branch at :527, and every later commit returns (remaining>=1, capture) at :543. The documented bound does not hold: the 30 s backstop at :1221-1226 measures silence from lastLiveEditTickAt, which :2052 refreshes on EVERY non-commit tick and :453 refreshes on every beginLiveEdit — so continued slider use keeps the stale capture alive indefinitely. Reachable trigger, all lines verified: (1) thumb A drags the height slider on drop X — ARScreen.swift:504 → :452 held=1, :454 capture=X; (2) the other hand taps the viewfinder — ARScreen.swift:110-118 toggles hudHidden, ARScreen.swift:143 removes hudOverlay and with it adjustPanel (ARScreen.swift:288-292), the Slider leaves the tree, ARScreen.swift:506's onEditingChanged(false) never fires → held stuck at 1, capture stuck at X; (3) tap again to restore the HUD; (4) updateNearest :1698 returns early forever, so nearestDrop stays X while the user walks to drop Y; (5) the user drags any slider — :452 held=2, :454 no-op, :2048 editTarget(capture:X, held:true) = X — and releases: :2058 commitBookkeeping(2, X, X) → (1, X), capture survives, held never returns to 0. Every subsequent edit in the session lands on X. The same alternate triggers exist via ARScreen.swift:289's `manager.renderedDropCount > 0` and the `!demoing` conjunct, which also tear the panel down without a commit.
findings.harm: Silent wrong-drop live edit PERSISTED to disk and Firestore — the exact STATE-L1 harm the wave has spent rounds 3, 4 and 5 killing, on the build that is about to go to the owner's field sessions. Field-visible signature: after an accidental viewfinder tap during a slider drag, the HUD distance/title readout stops following the user (it is pinned to X), "Place on ground" and "Pin to a spot" retarget X (both resolve `nearestDrop` at :2185/:2274), and dragging a slider in front of drop Y moves nothing on screen while X — possibly out of view, possibly out of sight entirely — is mutated and committed with library.update(persist: true) at :2144. Recovery requires a tab switch (:640 markCameraHidden → cancelLiveEdit), 30 s of not touching any slider, or walking far enough that the :1941 reconcile prunes X (:1942 removePerDropState) — i.e. the harm window is precisely the radius in which the user has OTHER drops to mis-edit. Neither FT-40 nor FT-3 exercises a mid-drag HUD-hide, so the field protocol as written will not catch it either.
findings.fix: One line at the choke point, in the round's own style: attach `.onDisappear { manager.cancelLiveEdit() }` to `adjustPanel` at ARScreen.swift:290. That single site covers all four teardown paths (hudHidden at :143, `!demoing` and `nearestDrop != nil` and `renderedDropCount > 0` at :288-292) and is unconditionally correct — a gesture whose control has left the screen is by definition abandoned, which is exactly cancelLiveEdit's contract at :457-459. Do NOT revert the round-5 fix: round 4's unconditional clear WAS F-D4-01. Optionally belt-and-braces in the manager: in beginLiveEdit (:451-455), when the capture is non-nil but the captured id is no longer `nearestDrop?.id` and no tick has arrived since the previous gesture ended, re-seat the capture — but the caller-side cancel is the honest fix and needs no heuristic.
findings.test_case: Two tests. (1) Caller-context, on the seam the counsel has demanded since F-D4-CTX: construct GeoARSessionManager with a recording DropLibrary stub and a driveable location double, drops X (nearest) then Y. beginLiveEdit(); adjustNearestDrop(height: 5, commit: false); then simulate the teardown by calling NOTHING (no commit, no cancel — that is the leak); drive the location so Y becomes geo-nearest; pump one 400 ms tick; beginLiveEdit(); adjustNearestDrop(height: 9, commit: true). ASSERT: the stub recorded an update for Y with height 9 and X received NO second update; and heldGestures is back to 0 after the commit. This test FAILS on abe4f50 (X gets the edit, Y gets nothing, counter stuck at 1) and passes once the onDisappear cancel lands. (2) XCUITest end-to-end on device, cheap and no seam required: start a height-slider drag, tap the viewfinder with a second touch, tap again to restore the HUD, walk (or mock-move) to a second drop, drag the slider, force-quit, relaunch — assert the SECOND drop's height changed and the first drop's did not. Add the same three steps as a FT-40 addendum so the field sessions cover the interaction even before the unit seam exists.

The two new CommitBookkeepingTests (:526-547, :549-563) exercise only the pure function GeoARSessionManager.commitBookkeeping (:538-544); `grep -rn 'GeoARSessionManager(' AugmentMeRealityTests/` returns zero hits, so no test reads editingDropID, heldGestures or liveEditingDrops through the manager, and the wiring at :2051-2062 is unguarded. Demonstration: re-add `if editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil }` to the end of applyEdit's commit block (:2151-2163) while leaving commitBookkeeping and its call site untouched — F-D4-01 is completely restored and the suite stays 149/149. This is F-D4-CTX (round-4 MEDIUM, 'Wave E acceptable if round 5 stays surgical') now standing as the guard-of-record on the round's own blocker fix, for the fourth consecutive round in which every escape was a correct pure function evaluated against wrong caller state.
findings.harm: The counsel's converged round-4 test design for F-D4-01 ('construct the REAL GeoARSessionManager with a recording stub DropLibrary + driveable location double... assert Y NEVER received an update') was not built, so nothing mechanically prevents round 6's fix from re-seeding the same defect class a fifth time — which F-D5-01 shows has already happened once in this round. Field-side, the only guards on the wrong-drop family are FT-40 and FT-3 (RSCH4-06), neither of which drives two thumbs or a mid-drag panel teardown.
findings.fix: Land the seam the counsel has now asked for twice, at the smaller of its two forms: extract the gesture state machine as a value type `GestureBinding { begin(nearest:) / tick(nearest:) -> UUID? / commit(nearest:) -> UUID? / cancel() }` owning (capture, heldGestures, lastTickAt), have the manager hold one and delegate at :2048-2061, :451-455 and :460-465, and table-test it: two-thumb interleave, authored-snap-mid-drag, leaked-begin (the F-D5-01 sequence), removal-mid-gesture. Roughly 40 lines of extraction with no behaviour change, and it converts every finding in this family from 'traced by reading' to 'asserted'.
findings.test_case: GestureBindingTests: (a) begin→begin→commit→tick→commit asserts the tick between the two commits returns the ORIGINAL id even when `nearest` is passed as a different id, and that the capture is nil only after the second commit; (b) begin→tick→<teardown: no commit>→begin→tick asserts the second tick returns the NEW nearest, not the leaked capture (fails today, the F-D5-01 guard); (c) begin→authoredCommit(otherId)→tick asserts the gesture's capture is untouched; (d) commit with count already 0 asserts the count floors and the capture clears. Each of (a)-(d) trips a named assertion against a specific historical regression (round 3's boolean, round 4's tail, round 5's leak, round 3's F-D3-03 hoist).

findings.claim: commitBookkeeping's `&& capture == id` conjunct at :542 is dead at its only call site, because :2051 assigns `editingDropID = id` unconditionally two statements before the :2058 call and nothing between them can change it (:2052 writes only lastLiveEditTickAt, and only when !commit). The third assertion of testCaptureSurvivesUntilTheLastFingerLifts — `XCTAssertEqual(foreign.capture, capture)` at WaveDTests.swift:546, fed heldGestures:1, capture:X, committed: a fresh UUID — therefore guards a state that production cannot reach: exactly the 'table rows guarding dead code' shape this same round deleted from editTarget as F-D4-DEADPARAM. Unlike that case the right resolution is NOT deletion: :2051 is load-bearing (with capture nil and held==2, the first commit's :2051 is what ESTABLISHES the freeze for the surviving second finger; remove it and F-D4-01 returns by another door), and the conjunct keeps the pure function total.
findings.harm: None at runtime. The cost is epistemic and it is the cost that has driven this whole wave: a reader auditing round 6 sees a guarded branch and a green table row and concludes the wrong-id case is defended in production, when it is unreachable — the same false confidence the round-4 verdict called out one function over.
findings.fix: Two lines of doc, no code change: on commitBookkeeping (:531-537) state the call-site invariant explicitly ('at the sole call site :2058, `capture` is invariantly `id` because :2051 rebinds it first; the conjunct keeps the function total and would matter to any future second caller'), and add the same one-line note above WaveDTests.swift:543 so the `foreign` row is labelled as a totality row rather than read as a production guard.
findings.test_case: Not a new test — a label on an existing one. If the counsel prefers the row to be live rather than annotated, the seam from F-D5-03 makes it live for free: GestureBinding.commit(id:) called with an id that differs from the stored capture is reachable in the value-type formulation (authoredCommit vs gesture commit), and the row then guards real behaviour.

test_vacuity.reason: NON-VACUOUS against the RULE, VACUOUS against the DEFECT. Rule side: if the round-4 semantics were re-expressed inside commitBookkeeping (:542 becomes `let captureClears = capture == id`, dropping the `remaining == 0` conjunct), the first call returns (1, nil) and `XCTAssertEqual(first.capture, capture, "capture must outlive the first commit")` at :535 TRIPS — that is the assertion, named. A literal revert of the round-5 commit deletes the function entirely and the test fails to compile, which the suite also catches. Defect side: F-D4-01 lived in the CALL SITE, not the rule. Keep commitBookkeeping and its :2058 call exactly as shipped and re-add `if editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil }` at the end of applyEdit's commit block (:2151-2163): the bug is 100% restored and this test — and all 149 — stay green. Third assertion `XCTAssertEqual(foreign.capture, capture)` (:546) is vacuous outright: :2051 makes `capture != id` unreachable at the only call site (F-D5-02).

Partially. `XCTAssertEqual(stray.remainingHeld, 0)` at :556 and `XCTAssertEqual(again.remainingHeld, 0)` at :562 are real: drop the `max(0, ...)` at :541 and both trip with -1. That restores the round-3 hygiene bar the round-4 verdict asked for. But `XCTAssertNil(stray.capture)` at :557 is VACUOUS — the input capture is already nil, so it holds under any implementation that returns either the input or nil, including a deliberately broken one. The production shape of a stray commit is (heldGestures: 0, capture: X, committed: X) — a lost begin event while a capture from the previous gesture is still inside its 1.5 s window (:476) — and that case, where the interesting question is whether the capture clears, is not exercised. One extra call with capture: X asserting nil would make the assertion earn its place.

VACUOUS AS A GUARD ON THIS ROUND'S EDIT. The round-5 change to editTarget was the removal of a parameter that was a literal nil at its one call site (F-D4-DEADPARAM) — behaviour-preserving by construction — so there is nothing for a behavioural test to catch, and all four surviving assertions evaluate identically against the round-4 implementation (the `if let authored` branch at old :2036 is simply skipped when authored is nil). It also has zero bearing on F-D4-01: editTarget's binding table was never the defect. Separately, the test IS non-vacuous on editTarget's own STATE-L1 contract — `XCTAssertNil(GeoARSessionManager.editTarget(capture: nil, held: false, nearest: nearest))` at :480-482 trips the moment anyone restores an unheld-tick fallback to nearest, and the new capture-survives-finger-up row at :472-477 pins the 1.5 s-expiry semantics — so it should be kept, just not counted as coverage of anything this round changed.

Replaying reviewer C's trace line by line: session(_:didFailWithError:) :2841-2871 sets sessionFailed = true (:2846); with the tick already cancelled (F3 guard :2864, tickTask nil after suspendSession :424) it RETURNS without recovery, leaving pre-failure holders in placedHolders. closures.item: RSCH4-02 — MetricKit subscriber (Services/CrashDiagnostics.swift + AugmentMeRealityApp.init registration): would a crash on THIS build produce a debrief-able artifact on next launch?
closures.proof: Selector binding VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY, not assumed: the SDK declares the requirement as `- (void)didReceiveDiagnosticPayloads:(NSArray<MXDiagnosticPayload *> *)payloads` with no NS_SWIFT_NAME (iPhoneOS26.5.sdk/…/MetricKit.framework/Headers/MXMetricManager.h, @optional block), and I compiled and ran an exact structural copy of the class (final NSObject + MXMetricManagerSubscriber + Sendable, `func didReceive(_ payloads: [MXDiagnosticPayload])`): `responds(to: Selector("didReceiveDiagnosticPayloads:")) == true`. So Swift's omit-needless-words import plus @objc inference from the optional protocol requirement does wire it — the method WILL be invoked. Registration window: AugmentMeRealityApp.init :12-24 calls CrashDiagnostics.shared.start() (:23) → MXMetricManager.shared.add(self) (:28), i.e. inside @main App init on the main thread, before any scene connects, so it precedes the next-launch delivery window; the subscriber is a `static let shared` singleton so MetricKit's subscriber table cannot outlive it. didReceive (:31-45) touches only `log` (Logger, Sendable), locals, and FileManager — no main-actor state — matching the header's "This method is invoked on a background queue." Sendable conformance is sound under SE-0302: final class, single stored property `let log: Logger` (Sendable), superclass NSObject (the permitted superclass) — consistent with the leg-5 report of 0 diagnostics for this file. Persistence: diagnosticsDirectory() (:47-56) creates Application Support/diagnostics with withIntermediateDirectories: true, which also creates Application Support itself (iOS does not pre-create it), then `payload.jsonRepresentation()` (imported from `- (NSData *)JSONRepresentation`, MXDiagnosticPayload.h:79) is written with .atomic. `crashDiagnostics`/`hangDiagnostics` are correctly treated as optional (`nullable` NSArray in MXDiagnosticPayload.h:48,:60). Deployment target 17.0 (project.pbxproj:269 et al.) clears MXDiagnosticPayload's iOS 14 / MXHangDiagnostic's iOS 14 floors. reviews.ship_opinion: Round 5 is close-able, and my three assigned items are genuinely closed at mechanism level: the TTFO re-arm sits where placements die, so no restorer ordering can decide it and reviewer C's false-latch trace is dead on every reachable ordering; the detach instrument is at the one choke point that covers all six sites, is edge-only, cannot claim a toggle the guard refused, and still matches the documented subsystem-filtered field grep at default log level; and the MetricKit subscriber is real code that will actually be invoked — I verified the `didReceiveDiagnosticPayloads:` selector binding empirically against the iOS 26.5 SDK rather than trusting the Swift signature. That keeps the cross-thread exercise of `stateLock`, removes the off-main ARView write production never performs, and eliminates the main-blocked-in-group.wait hang class. findings.claim: Leg 3's round-5 restatement — "**no in-app lock is acquired while `stateLock` is held**" — is FALSE, and is contradicted by the file it certifies and by its own parenthetical two clauses later. SemanticOcclusionPass.encode holds stateLock from :276 to function exit (defer :277) and inside that region acquires SemanticFeed.lock via feed.snapshot() at :298 and MidFieldDepthFeed.lock via midDepthFeed?.snapshot(forFrameAt:maxAge:) at :323. findings.harm: Field-measurable via the next maintainer, not the next frame. validations.claim: (1a) `grep -c 'ThreadSanitizer:' <log> == 0` is the right evidence form for any TSan leg, rather than a test pass count.
validations.basis: xcodebuild(1) (keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/xcodebuild.1.html) documents `-enableThreadSanitizer YES/NO` as a scheme override and specifies NO exit-code contract for sanitizer reports; sanitizer runtimes default to halt_on_error=0 (report-and-continue) and write reports to stderr, so a race can be reported while every XCTest case still passes and the action still exits 0. A textual grep over the full log is the only artifact independent of runner exit-code propagation. Choosing the bare token `ThreadSanitizer:` rather than `ThreadSanitizer: data race` is also correct — it additionally catches `lock-order-inversion`, `double lock of a mutex`, `signal-unsafe call`, `data race on vptr`, `heap-use-after-free`, which are exactly the report classes this wave's lock discipline could produce.

validations.claim: (1a) `SIMCTL_CHILD_TSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1` actually delivers TSAN_OPTIONS into the simulator test process launched by `xcodebuild test`.
validations.basis: xcodebuild(1) documents exactly one mechanism for this: "Set an environment variable whose name is prefixed with TEST_RUNNER_ to have that variable passed, with its prefix stripped, to all test runner processes launched during a test action" (e.g. `TEST_RUNNER_TSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 xcodebuild test …`). The man page contains no mention of SIMCTL_CHILD_. `SIMCTL_CHILD_` is documented only in `xcrun simctl help launch/spawn` — simctl reads it from ITS OWN environment and applies it to the process simctl spawns (or to launchd_sim when simctl itself boots the device). `xcodebuild test` does not shell out to the simctl CLI, and if the device was already booted the variable never reaches launchd_sim at all. So the recorded prefix is at best undocumented and most likely a no-op. IMPORTANT: this does not invalidate the round-5 evidence — halt_on_error is a belt-and-braces amplifier and the grep is the load-bearing artifact, unaffected either way. What must change is the record's phrasing, which asserts a sanitizer configuration that (i) was probably never in effect and (ii) a clean run cannot falsify, since with zero reports halt_on_error is unobservable. Fix: re-word to TEST_RUNNER_, or drop the clause and let the grep stand alone; a temporarily-enabled deliberate-race test is the only positive control that proves the runtime is configured as claimed.

validations.basis: The core is right: in Swift 5 language mode `complete` is warning-only with no runtime or codegen change; the same violations become errors only under SWIFT_VERSION 6. But it is set on Release as well as Debug (project.pbxproj:396), and three non-diagnostic risks follow and are unrecorded. (a) BUILD-AVAILABILITY: the SendNonSendable/RegionAnalysis pass now runs on the shipping lane, and that pass has a live family of ICE reports (swiftlang #74458, #75468, #77942, #85329, and #88173 — a crash in the performance inliner with concurrency features at -O, i.e. specifically the optimized Release configuration). This project has already hit one ICE in this pass class. Failure mode: the RELEASE build stops compiling after an Xcode upgrade, not merely an audit lane. Recovery is deleting one line, but it should be an explicitly accepted risk with the escape named. (b) FUTURE DEFAULT SHIFT: the concrete one is SWIFT_VERSION 5.0 → 6.0, which promotes today's 114 warnings to 114 errors — the Wave E migration is now gated by this setting rather than optional. Xcode 26 additionally ships SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY=YES and SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION=MainActor as defaults for NEW projects only (donnywals.com/setting-default-actor-isolation-in-xcode-26); this is an existing project, so it retains `nonisolated` default and no silent behavior shift occurs today. (c) MASKING: 114 permanent warnings in every build is a noise floor a NEW concurrency warning disappears into, and any future SWIFT_TREAT_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS breaks Release. Ruling: KEEP the pin — a continuously-live audit is worth more than a one-shot lane — but record (a)–(c) as accepted, with the 114 as a ratchet baseline re-counted each wave.

validations.claim: (1d) The 114-diagnostic count methodology (grep `warning:` filtered to /AugmentMeReality/ paths, sort -u) has no systematic undercount.

Two REAL undercounts exist. (i) REPRODUCIBILITY — the record pins neither CLEAN-vs-incremental nor the configuration. Swift emits diagnostics only for files it actually recompiles, so any incremental re-run collapses the count toward 0; and Debug (per-file, incremental) versus Release (whole-module) run region analysis over different unit boundaries and produce genuinely different diagnostic sets. Without `clean` and a named configuration recorded beside it, 114 is not reproducible and cannot serve as the Wave E ratchet it is meant to be. (ii) ESCAPE HATCHES — five first-party types are declared `@unchecked Sendable`: SemanticFeed (AR/SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:12), SemanticOcclusionPass (:70), MidFieldDepthFeed (AR/MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:9), SourceBox (:201), SeenGeometryBox (AR/GeospatialEngine.swift:434). `@unchecked` is precisely the annotation that switches OFF the stored-property Sendability checking leg 5 claims to perform, and it is applied to the class at the epicenter of this wave. Minor third: the `/AugmentMeReality/` path filter drops diagnostics with no file location (module/driver level) and any in generated sources under DerivedData. validations.claim: RSCH4-02 (MetricKit): MXCrashDiagnostic/MXHangDiagnostic persistence at Application Support is the right minimal shape, and MetricKit will serve as the instrument for the 99.5% bar.
validations.basis: SHAPE: largely right. `MXMetricManagerSubscriber` with both diagnostic types, registered in the App's `init` before the first scene (App/AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:19) — correct, since a late or conditional subscriber drops next-launch payloads; `didReceive` runs on MetricKit's own queue and touches only locals + FileManager, no shared mutable state (Services/CrashDiagnostics.swift:31-46); payload persisted whole via `jsonRepresentation()` so nothing is lost to a lossy schema; os_log key on the app subsystem, honoring the RSCH-2 lesson. Two LOW warts: `ISO8601DateFormatter()` filenames embed colons (legal in POSIX paths, displayed as '/' in Finder and a portability wart on export) and two payloads sharing a `timeStampEnd` second overwrite each other via the `.atomic` write to the same URL; and there is no pruning, so Application Support/diagnostics grows unbounded and is iCloud-backed by default. DELIVERY — the material correction: MetricKit does not deliver diagnostic payloads to development builds installed from Xcode; delivery requires TestFlight or App Store distribution (Apple Developer Forums threads 730975 and 765149; delivery cadence is metrics ≤ once/day, diagnostics immediately on iOS 15+/macOS 12+ for those channels; forum 806457 documents a further iOS 17.2–17.5 regression where crash/hang diagnostics were not returned at all, fixed by iOS 18/26 — this project's iOS 26.5 target is clear of it). Consequence the record must state: the four Wave D field sessions run an Xcode-installed build of abe4f50, so `CrashDiagnostics` will produce ZERO payloads during them, and MXHangDiagnostic — pitched in the record as 'the one instrument that catches a main actor blocked behind stateLock' — is NOT available in this build's sessions. DENOMINATOR: a crash-free PERCENTAGE needs one, and `CrashDiagnostics` implements only the `[MXDiagnosticPayload]` overload (:31), not `[MXMetricPayload]`, so no MXAppRunTimeMetric/MXAppLaunchMetric is captured; MetricKit payloads also arrive only from users with analytics sharing enabled (community-measured opt-in around 25%, chimehq.com/blog/metrickit-crash-reporting). MetricKit alone therefore yields a biased numerator with no denominator and can never produce a 99.5% ratio. The record's 'the mechanism that will eventually sign it landed in round 5' overstates what landed.

own_findings.claim: The 114 count is not reproducible from the record: neither the build configuration nor a clean-build guarantee is stated. Swift emits diagnostics only for files it actually recompiles, so any incremental re-run reports dramatically fewer; and Debug (per-file, incremental) versus Release (whole-module) run region analysis over different unit boundaries and produce genuinely different diagnostic sets.
own_findings.harm: 114 is meant to be the Wave E ratchet baseline. A future re-count that reads 40 will be indistinguishable from real migration progress when it may simply be an incremental build, or the other configuration — and a count that silently drifts downward is a report that says the Swift-6 debt is shrinking when nothing has been fixed. The same ambiguity would let a real regression (a new crossing introduced in Wave E) hide inside a number nobody can reproduce.
own_findings.fix: Record the exact command beside the number in DECISIONS.md — `xcodebuild clean build -project … -scheme … -configuration <Debug|Release> -destination … 2>&1 | grep 'warning:' | grep '/AugmentMeReality/' | sort -u | wc -l` — and add one clause stating that 114 is a FLOOR, not a census, because region-based isolation reports the first violation per region and fixing one can reveal more.

own_findings.claim: The MetricKit instrument that closed RSCH4-02 cannot produce a crash-free RATIO, and will not fire at all during Wave D's field sessions. MetricKit does not deliver diagnostic payloads to development builds installed from Xcode — delivery requires TestFlight or App Store distribution (Apple Developer Forums 730975, 765149). Separately, Services/CrashDiagnostics.swift implements only `didReceive(_ payloads: [MXDiagnosticPayload])` (:31) and not the `[MXMetricPayload]` overload, so no MXAppRunTimeMetric or MXAppLaunchMetric is ever captured.
own_findings.harm: Two concrete consequences. (i) The four Wave D sessions run an Xcode-installed build of abe4f50, so CrashDiagnostics produces zero payloads during them — and MXHangDiagnostic, which DECISIONS.md:1204 pitches as 'the one instrument that catches a main actor blocked behind stateLock, which renderFPS's 2-second mean smears away', is therefore unavailable in precisely the sessions that were meant to look for it. The specific Wave D failure shape stays unmeasured. (ii) Post-TestFlight, the record's 'the mechanism that will eventually sign it landed in round 5' will not hold: crash payloads arrive only from users with analytics sharing enabled (community-measured opt-in around 25%, chimehq.com/blog/metrickit-crash-reporting), giving a biased numerator with no denominator at all. A percentage cannot be computed from it.
own_findings.fix: Three parts, all small. (1) Implement the `didReceive(_ payloads: [MXMetricPayload])` overload and persist MXAppRunTimeMetric/MXAppLaunchMetric alongside the diagnostics, so the bar becomes crashes-per-foreground-hour — a defensible surrogate the app can compute from its own data. (2) Add one sentence to DECISIONS.md stating that MetricKit is TestFlight/App-Store-only and is therefore inert in the Wave D sessions, so nobody later reads the sessions' silence as evidence of zero crashes or zero hangs. (3) For the sessions themselves, substitute the free on-device instrument: iOS Settings → Developer → Hang Detection, which raises a live banner on a main-thread stall — add it to the S3/S4 setup steps in the new FIELDTESTS.md section. Non-gating for the desk: the 99.5% bar is already explicitly deferred post-TestFlight.

own_findings.claim: The leg-1 evidence line asserts a sanitizer configuration that was probably never in effect: `SIMCTL_CHILD_TSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1` in front of `xcodebuild test`. The documented mechanism for getting an environment variable into an xcodebuild test-runner process is the TEST_RUNNER_ prefix (xcodebuild(1)); SIMCTL_CHILD_ is documented only for `xcrun simctl` launch/spawn/boot, and xcodebuild does not go through the simctl CLI.
own_findings.harm: A clean run cannot falsify the claim — with zero reports, halt_on_error is unobservable — so the next round will inherit 'halt_on_error was on' as established fact and may lean on it (for instance, treating a green suite as proof no report was swallowed mid-run). The evidence itself is unharmed, because the grep is the load-bearing artifact and is independent of halt_on_error; only the record's assertion is wrong.
own_findings.fix: Re-word the evidence line to `TEST_RUNNER_TSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1` and state explicitly that the grep is the load-bearing artifact either way. If the wave wants the halt_on_error claim to be more than decoration, the only positive control is a temporarily-enabled deliberate-race test that MUST abort the run — otherwise drop the clause and let the grep stand alone.

It is the least-bad available epoch (the pre-reset epoch belongs to a session that died), so this is a disclosure issue, not a defect.

WHICH BAR EACH REMAINING SESSION MEASURES. S1 (desk gate, already executed on abe4f50: legs 1 and 5 plus 149/149): measures NO bar — it is a precondition, not evidence. S2 (device ASan/UBSan/Guard-Malloc, correctness only): measures NO bar — no performance number is valid under 2–3× CPU; it is leg-2 evidence toward the stability argument alone. S3 (FT-28 + FT-40 + FT-3 + FT-41 + touched paths, recorder ON except during the FT-28 fps window): measures bar 2 (≥30 fps, with p95 ≤ 40 ms as the teeth) and bar 3 (thermal — not .serious at 10 minutes), contributes scrubbed video toward bar 4 for every occlusion pass it runs, and carries the non-optional regression cases. S4 (FT-31 70-minute soak plus ten resume observations scrubbed on video, recorder OFF during the hour): measures bar 3 across the hour and bar 4 from the scrubbed resume observations, and is leg 4 of RENDER-1. Bar 1 (99.5% crash-free) is measured by NO session and must not appear as met in the closing ADR.

THE NON-OPTIONAL FIELD CASES. FT-40 (GROUND-SNAP) and FT-3 (tab flip) remain non-optional because they are the ONLY guards on the two round-3 blockers closed in round 4: no test constructs GeoARSessionManager or the session holder, so the flagship 'Place on ground' path (F-D3-01) and the warm-resume visibility path (F-D3-02) have zero automated coverage — a failure on either re-opens the wave. FT-41 must join them as a third, for the identical reason applied to round 5's own blocker fix: the pure function is guarded, the wiring and the harm path are not.

BARS THIS BUILD'S INSTRUMENTS STILL CANNOT MEASURE. (1) 99.5% crash-free — no fleet, no denominator, and MetricKit is inert in an Xcode-installed build; correctly re-scoped as a post-TestFlight statistic, and the closing ADR must say so in those words. (2) A main actor blocked behind stateLock — the specific Wave D shape MXHangDiagnostic was landed to catch will not fire in these sessions, and renderFPS's 2-second mean smears a sub-second stall; the free substitute is iOS Settings → Developer → Hang Detection during S3/S4, which is why it belongs in the checklist. (3) The renderCallbacks slot-assignment race — unmeasurable by construction: TSan cannot run where RealityKit's render thread does, ASan cannot see inside uninstrumented RealityKit, and the round-5 probe creates no second accessor of those slots. It stays 'mitigated, not proven', now dischargeable via the Feedback Assistant report once filed. (4) Bar 4 (zero draw-over) is measurable only from scrubbed video and is therefore unmeasurable as the checklist stands today — it becomes measurable the moment F-R5-02 lands, which is exactly why that edit is blocking.

RULING: land the two FIELDTESTS.md edits, then the sessions may run on abe4f50 unchanged. If both blocking items land as described, I have no further desk objection and the wave should proceed to the owner's field sessions without a round 6.
